newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Oct 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Oct 31.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO DAILY -- Chinese dissident Wang Dan was sentenced to 11 years in prison. Hong Kong's Democratic Party planned to protest the verdict.

-- Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO -- Members of the China's Preparatory Committee will vote to choose 400 members of the Selection Committee, which in turn will select Hong Kong's first Chief Executive after the handover next year.
-- Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO -- China to make use of foreign investments to further urban development.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Chinese and Hong Kong finance officials denied having heard of a contingency fund prepared to help stabilise Hong Kong's stock market.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- The fourth round of Hong Kong-U.S. textiles negotiations ended without any substantial achievements.

-- HONG KONG COMMERCIAL DAILY -- The price of a public minibus has gone up to HK$3.3 million from HK$2.2 million in the past year. Some minibus groups worried licence speculation would lead to an increase in operation cost.

-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Cathay Pacific Airways would be hit by departures of two of its most senior financial figures after last month's reorganisation of its general management ranks.
-- China's Tsinlien Co will acquire light industrial companies for its listing in Hong Kong.
-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD -- Analysts predicted limited impact from a mainland contingency fund meant to ward off stock market volatility.
-- About 20 small brokers have expressed interest in merging to form a listing vehicle to compete with large foreign brokerages.
